faq.q: Why did my pet have to die?
faq.a: All living things die one day, and most pets have shorter lives than people. Pets usually die from old age, an illness or an accident. It is not because of anything you did.

faq.q: Is it silly to cry so much over a pet?
faq.a: Not at all. Your pet was your friend and part of your family, so of course you feel sad. Grown-ups cry over pets too.
asks: Is it okay to cry when a pet dies?

faq.q: How can I say goodbye to my pet?
faq.a: You could plant a flower, draw a picture, write a letter, make a photo book or hold a small goodbye with your family where everyone shares a favourite memory.
asks: How can I remember my pet?

faq.q: Should we get a new pet straight away?
faq.a: There is no rule. Some families wait until the sadness feels softer. A new pet will not replace your old one, but it can be loved in its own way.
asks: When can we get another pet?

faq.q: Was it my fault that my pet died?
faq.a: Almost always, no. Vets and families do their best, and many illnesses cannot be stopped. If you keep worrying about it, tell a grown-up you trust.

facts: Cats often live 12 to 18 years, while hamsters usually live only about 2 to 3 years.
Child experts advise using clear words like "died" with children, because phrases like "went to sleep" can be confusing or frightening.
